newsitem.title: USA: New Energy to buy power from Bonneville -- WSJ.
newsitem.headline: New Energy to buy power from Bonneville -- WSJ.

text.p: Electricity broker New Energy Ventures Inc will announce it has agreed to buy up to $500 million of power from the federal Bonneville Power Administration, The Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday.
The pact is expected to be announced on Tuesday. It is the first major transaction under California's sweeping December 1995 restructuring of its $20 billion power market.

The deal is a significant step toward transforming California's monopoly power market. California has been dominated by investor-owned power firms and municipal utilities that have exclusive franchises for their service areas.

Changes to federal law mandated free-market sales to power resellers, but states were left with jurisdiction over sales to end-users. The changes have spawned an industry of electricity brokers such as New Energy, which hope to make money by buying and selling electricity more cheaply than the local utility.
New Energy was formed in 1995 and got $1 million in startup funding from Tucson Electric Power Co with an option to buy up to a 50 percent stake.

The deal calls for New Energy to buy 200 megawatts of surplus electricity from Bonneville for five years starting Jan 1, 1998. New Energy also has an option for another 200 megawatts over the same period.
New Energy's clients include two big power-buying groups - the Association of Bay Area Governments and the Southern California Cities Joint Powers Consortium.
